entities.name: Achille Delaere
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Achille Delaere (1866–1925) was a Belgian Missionary of the Immaculate Heart of Mary (CICM, known as Scheut Missionaries) who worked in China during the late Qing dynasty and early Republican period. Born in Kortrijk, he joined the Scheut congregation and was assigned to Inner Mongolia, one of the most challenging mission territories in East Asia.

Delaere served in Inner Mongolia through decades of extraordinary upheaval: the Boxer Uprising of 1900, the collapse of the Qing dynasty in 1912, and the chaos of warlord-era China. He established parishes, schools, and medical stations in areas where Catholic presence was precarious and often violently contested. The Scheut missionaries' work in Inner Mongolia was characterised by close engagement with Mongolian nomadic culture and the creation of local institutions designed to outlast foreign missionary presence.

His contribution exemplifies the ambiguous legacy of Belgian Catholic missions in China: simultaneously agents of European cultural influence and founders of indigenous Christian communities that would survive the expulsion of foreign missionaries after 1949. The Church in Inner Mongolia today traces its institutional roots in part to the patient work of missionaries like Delaere, who spent their lives far from Europe building parishes that would eventually become part of a Chinese-led Church.
